answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates the strongest pull toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that carries explicit downstream damage: deep discounting bought trial starts (+31%) and a one-quarter revenue bump (+18%) while adding 12pp of renewal churn in small accounts — exactly the segment under attack. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a negative-value trade dressed as a win, so I decline the discount even though it is the most topically responsive move. The two measured declines (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are plausibly one causal chain: memory_86 ties shortened onboarding to completion, time-to-value, and downstream adoption, which makes onboarding the upstream lever and activation_messaging (memory_91) the more downstream patch. I therefore spend the slot on simplify_onboarding and spend verification on the two memories I am actually leaning on rather than on memory_73, whose harm is already visible in the summary. What I need from the archive is the part compression stripped out: memory_86's summary asserts a lift but names no effect size, duration, or whether the adoption gain persisted past week one; memory_31 says 'durable' but a day-12 consolidation cannot have observed durability over a long horizon, and it does not say which fields were cut. Both are old (day 12 and day 52) and were measured before a competitor reshaped the SMB mix, so prior effect sizes may not transfer. Two named risks I am carrying rather than resolving: cutting required signup fields can strip the firmographic data that routes enterprise prospects into the sales-assisted path memory_44 says converts better on pipeline quality, so a self-serve activation win could quietly cannibalize higher-quality pipeline; and completion-rate lift can be an artifact of asking less rather than delivering value sooner. I run this as a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, holding out a control and instrumenting qualified-pipeline and enterprise-routing rate alongside completion and activation, so a gain in the headline metric that arrives with a loss in lead quality is detectable before it is shipped. If the archive shows memory_31's lift was short-lived or that the removed fields were the qualification fields, I fall back to activation_messaging, which addresses the larger decline without touching lead capture.
